units.1 Maccabees 9:18: Judas fell, and the rest fled.
units.1 Maccabees 9:19: Jonathan and Simon took up Judas their brother and buried him in the tomb of his fathers in Modein.
units.1 Maccabees 9:20: They wept for him, and all Israel lamented him with a great lament. They mourned for many days and said,
units.1 Maccabees 9:21: “How has the mighty one fallen, the saviour of Israel!”
units.1 Maccabees 9:22: The rest of the deeds of Judas, his battles, the brave deeds he performed, and his greatness were not written down, for they were exceedingly many.
units.1 Maccabees 9:23: After the death of Judas, the lawless emerged throughout all Israel’s territory, and all who practiced injustice rose up.
units.1 Maccabees 9:24: In those days an exceedingly great famine occurred, and the country went over to their side.
units.2 Maccabees 2:19: The events concerning Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, the purification of the greatest temple and the dedication of the altar,
units.2 Maccabees 2:20: and also the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes and his son Eupator,
units.2 Maccabees 2:21: and the manifestations from heaven to those who zealously performed brave deeds for Judaism, so that, although few, they plundered the whole land and pursued the barbarian multitudes,
units.2 Maccabees 2:22: recovered the temple renowned throughout the inhabited world, freed the city, and restored the laws that were about to be abolished, the Lord having become merciful to them with all gentleness—
units.2 Maccabees 2:23: these things, set forth by Jason of Cyrene in five books, we shall attempt to abridge into one composition.
units.2 Maccabees 2:24: For, seeing the abundance of figures and the difficulty caused by the mass of material for those who wish to enter into the narratives of the history,
units.2 Maccabees 2:25: we have taken thought for the pleasure of those who wish to read, for the ease of those eager to commit it to memory, and for the benefit of everyone who encounters it.
units.2 Maccabees 2:26: For us who have undertaken the hard work of abridgement, the task is not easy; it involves sweat and sleeplessness.
units.2 Maccabees 2:27: Just as it is not easy for someone preparing a banquet and seeking others’ benefit, nevertheless, for the gratitude of the many, we will gladly bear the hard work.
units.2 Maccabees 2:28: We leave the precise treatment of each matter to the historian, while labouring to follow the outlines of the abridgement.
units.2 Maccabees 2:29: For just as the architect of a new house must consider its whole foundation, while the person undertaking its encaustic work and painting must examine what is suitable for decoration, so, I think, it is with us.
units.2 Maccabees 2:30: To enter deeply into matters, range widely in the discussion, and investigate the particulars belongs to the original historian.
units.2 Maccabees 2:31: But the person making a recasting should be permitted to pursue concise expression and set aside an exhaustive treatment of the subject.
units.2 Maccabees 2:32: Let us therefore begin the narrative here, adding only this much to what has already been said: it would be foolish to expand the preface to the history while abridging the history itself.
units.1 Maccabees 12:5: This is the copy of the letters Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
units.1 Maccabees 12:6: “Jonathan the high priest, the council of elders of the nation, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people, to the Spartans their brothers, greetings.
units.1 Maccabees 12:7: In former times letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Areus, who reigned among you, stating that you are our brothers, as the copy below shows.
units.1 Maccabees 12:8: Onias received the envoy with honour and accepted the letters, in which alliance and friendship were declared.
units.1 Maccabees 12:9: Although we have no need of these things, since we have as encouragement the holy books that are in our hands,
units.1 Maccabees 12:10: we have undertaken to send to renew brotherhood and friendship with you, so that we may not become estranged from you. For many seasons have passed since you sent to us.
units.1 Maccabees 12:11: We therefore remember you continually at every season, at the festivals and the other appointed days, in the sacrifices we offer and in our prayers, as it is right and fitting to remember brothers.
units.1 Maccabees 12:13: But many afflictions and many wars have surrounded us, and the kings around us have made war on us.
units.1 Maccabees 12:14: We did not wish to trouble you or our other allies and friends in these wars,
units.1 Maccabees 12:15: for we have help from Heaven helping us; we were rescued from our enemies, and our enemies were humbled.
units.1 Maccabees 12:16: We have therefore chosen Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason and sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.
units.1 Maccabees 12:17: We have also commanded them to go to you, greet you, and deliver our letters concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.
units.1 Maccabees 12:18: Now you will do well to answer us concerning these matters.”

units.1 Maccabees 13:19: He sent the children and the hundred talents, but Tryphon proved false and did not release Jonathan.
units.1 Maccabees 13:20: After this Tryphon came to invade the country and crush it. They went around by the road to Adora. Simon and his army moved opposite him wherever he went.
units.1 Maccabees 13:21: Those in the citadel sent envoys to Tryphon, urging him to come to them through the wilderness and send them food.
units.1 Maccabees 13:22: Tryphon prepared all his cavalry to go, but that night there was exceedingly heavy snow, and he did not go because of the snow. He set out and came to Gilead.
units.1 Maccabees 13:23: When he approached Bascama, he killed Jonathan, and Jonathan was buried there.
units.1 Maccabees 13:24: Tryphon turned and went away to his own land.

units.Ezra 6:1: Then Darius the king issued a decision and made a search in the libraries where the treasury is kept in Babylon.
units.Ezra 6:2: A scroll was found in a city, in the citadel of the city of the Medes, and this was written in it: “Memorandum:
units.Ezra 6:3: In the first year of Cyrus the king, King Cyrus issued a decision concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let the house be built, and the place where they sacrifice the sacrifices. He set an elevation: sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide,
units.Ezra 6:4: with three courses of strong stone and one wooden course. The expense will be paid from the king’s house.
units.Ezra 6:5: And let the silver and gold vessels of God’s house, which Nabouchodonosor took from the house in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, be given back and go to the sanctuary in Jerusalem, to the place where they were set in God’s house.”
units.Ezra 6:6: “Now you shall give, governors beyond the river, Satharbouzana and their fellow slaves the Apharsachaians beyond the river; keeping far away from there,
units.Ezra 6:7: leave the work on God’s house alone. Let the leaders of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build that house of God on its site.
units.Ezra 6:8: I have issued a decision that you must not do anything with the elders of the Jews concerning the building of that house of God. From the king’s resources, from the taxes beyond the river, let the expense be diligently supplied to those men, so that it is not stopped.
units.Ezra 6:9: Whatever may be lacking—offspring of cattle and of rams, and lambs for whole burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine and oil—let it be given to them day by day according to the word of the priests in Jerusalem, whatever they ask,
units.Ezra 6:10: so that they may offer sweet fragrances to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
units.Ezra 6:11: I have also issued a decision: for anyone who changes this word, a timber will be taken down from his house, and he will be raised upright and fastened upon it. His house will be dealt with according to me.
units.Ezra 6:12: The God whose name dwells there will overthrow every king and people who stretches out a hand to alter or destroy that house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued the decision; it shall be carried out diligently.”
units.1 Maccabees 15:25: On the second day King Antiochus encamped against Dora, continually bringing his forces against it, making siege engines, and blocking Tryphon from going out or coming in.
units.1 Maccabees 15:26: Simon sent him two thousand picked men to fight alongside him, along with silver, gold, and ample equipment.
units.1 Maccabees 15:27: He would not receive them, but annulled everything he had previously agreed with Simon and became estranged from him.
units.1 Maccabees 15:28: He sent Athenobius, one of his Friends, to confer with him, saying, “You hold Joppa, Gazara, and the citadel in Jerusalem, cities of my kingdom.
units.1 Maccabees 15:29: You have devastated their territories, inflicted a great blow upon the land, and gained control of many places in my kingdom.
units.1 Maccabees 15:30: Now, therefore, hand over the cities you have seized and the tribute of the places you have taken outside the borders of Judea.
units.1 Maccabees 15:31: Otherwise, give five hundred talents of silver in their place, and another five hundred talents for the destruction you have caused and the tribute of the cities. If not, we will come and make war on you.”
units.1 Maccabees 15:32: Athenobius, the king’s Friend, came to Jerusalem. He saw Simon’s glory, the display of gold and silver vessels, and the large retinue, and was astonished. He reported the king’s words to him.
units.1 Maccabees 15:33: Simon answered him, “We have neither taken foreign land nor gained control of others’ property, but the inheritance of our fathers, which our enemies unjustly seized at one time.
units.1 Maccabees 15:34: Now that we have the opportunity, we are holding fast to the inheritance of our fathers.
units.1 Maccabees 15:35: As for Joppa and Gazara, which you demand, these caused a great blow among the people and in our country. For these we will give a hundred talents.”
units.1 Maccabees 15:36: He did not answer him a word, but returned angrily to the king and reported these words, Simon’s glory, and everything he had seen. The king became greatly angry.
units.1 Kings 10:1: The queen of Sheba heard Solomon’s name and the Lord’s name, and came to test him with riddles.
units.1 Kings 10:2: She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels carrying spices, very much gold, and precious stones. She came in to Solomon and spoke to him about everything in her heart.
units.1 Kings 10:3: Solomon explained all her matters to her. No matter was overlooked by the king that he did not explain to her.
units.1 Kings 10:4: When the queen of Sheba saw all Solomon’s discernment and the house he had built,
units.1 Kings 10:5: Solomon’s food, the seating of his attendants, the station of his ministers, his clothing, his wine-pourers, and his whole burnt offering which he offered in the Lord’s house, she was beside herself.
units.1 Kings 10:6: She said to King Solomon, “The report I heard in my land about your word and your discernment is true.
units.1 Kings 10:7: I did not believe those speaking to me until I arrived and my eyes saw. Behold, it is not half as they reported to me! You have added good things beyond them, beyond every report I heard in my land.
units.1 Kings 10:8: Blessed are your women! Blessed are these attendants of yours who stand before you continually, hearing all your discernment!
units.1 Kings 10:9: Blessed be the Lord your God, who delighted in you, setting you on Israel’s throne! Because the Lord loves Israel, to establish them for ever, He made you king over them to carry out judgment in righteousness and in their judgments.”
units.1 Kings 10:10: She gave Solomon a hundred twenty talents of gold, very many spices, and precious stones. Never again came such an abundance of spices as the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
units.1 Kings 10:11: Hiram’s ship, which carried gold from Souphir, also brought a very great quantity of unhewn wood and precious stones.
units.1 Kings 10:12: The king made the unhewn wood into supports for the Lord’s house and the king’s house, and into harps and lyres for the singers. No such unhewn wood has come upon the earth or been seen anywhere to this day.
units.1 Kings 10:13: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she desired and asked for, besides everything he had given her through King Solomon’s hand. Then she returned and went to her land, she and all her attendants.
units.1 Maccabees 10:29: Now I release you and exempt all the Jews from tribute, the salt charge, and crown payments.
units.1 Maccabees 10:30: I relinquish from today onward the right to receive the third of the grain crop and the half of the fruit of the trees that fall to me, from the land of Judah and the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.
units.1 Maccabees 10:31: Let Jerusalem and its territory be holy and exempt, free of tithes and dues.
units.1 Maccabees 10:32: I also relinquish authority over the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it men of his own choosing to guard it.
units.1 Maccabees 10:33: Every Jewish person taken captive from the land of Judah into any part of my kingdom I release freely, without payment. Let all remit their taxes, including those upon their livestock.
units.1 Maccabees 10:34: Let all festivals, sabbaths, new moons, and appointed days, and the three days before a festival and the three after it, all be days of exemption and release for all Jews in my kingdom.
units.1 Maccabees 10:35: No one shall have authority to exact payment from or trouble any of them concerning any matter.
units.1 Maccabees 10:36: Let up to thirty thousand men of the Jews be enrolled in the king’s forces, and let allowances be given to them, as is proper for all the king’s forces.
units.1 Maccabees 10:37: Some of them shall be stationed in the king’s great strongholds, and some shall be appointed to positions of trust in the kingdom. Their supervisors and commanders shall be from among them, and they shall follow their own laws, as the king has also decreed in the land of Judah.
units.1 Maccabees 10:38: Let the three districts added to Judea from the region of Samaria be attached to Judea, so that they may be reckoned under one authority and obey no other authority except the high priest.
units.1 Maccabees 10:39: I have given Ptolemais and the territory belonging to it as a gift to the holy places in Jerusalem, for the expenses proper to the holy places.
units.1 Maccabees 10:40: I myself give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king’s accounts, from the appropriate places.
units.1 Maccabees 10:41: All the excess that they did not pay from the revenues as in former years they shall from now on give for the works of the house.
units.1 Maccabees 10:42: Besides these, the five thousand shekels of silver that they used to take from the revenues of the holy place from its account each year are also remitted, because they belong to the priests who minister.
units.1 Maccabees 10:43: All who flee to the temple in Jerusalem and anywhere within its precincts, owing royal dues or any other obligation, shall be released, together with all they possess in my kingdom.
units.1 Maccabees 10:44: The cost of rebuilding and renewing the works of the holy places shall be given from the king’s account.
units.1 Maccabees 10:45: The cost of rebuilding Jerusalem’s walls and fortifying it all around shall be given from the king’s account, and likewise for rebuilding walls in Judea.”

units.1 Kings 13:1: Behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the Lord’s word, while Jeroboam stood at the altar to offer sacrifice.
units.1 Kings 13:2: He called to the altar by the Lord’s word: “Altar, altar! Thus says the Lord: Behold, a son shall be born to David’s house, Josiah by name. He will sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifice upon you, and he will burn human bones upon you.”
units.1 Kings 13:3: He gave a portent that day, saying, “This is the word the Lord has spoken: Behold, the altar will split, and the fat upon it will pour out.”
units.1 Kings 13:4: When King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who had called against the altar in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” Behold, the hand he stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back.
units.1 Kings 13:5: The altar split, and the fat poured from the altar, according to the portent the man of God had given by the Lord’s word.
units.1 Kings 13:6: King Jeroboam said to the man of God, “Entreat the favor of the Lord your God, and let my hand be restored to me.” The man of God entreated the Lord’s favor, and he restored the king’s hand to him, so it became as it had been before.

units.2 Maccabees 8:1: Judas, also called Maccabeus, and those with him slipped secretly into the villages, called their kinsmen to join them, and gathered those who had remained in Judaism, assembling about six thousand.
units.2 Maccabees 8:2: They called upon the Lord to look upon the people trampled by everyone, and to have pity on the temple profaned by impious men,
units.2 Maccabees 8:3: to have mercy also on the city being destroyed and about to be levelled, and to listen to the blood crying out to Him,
units.2 Maccabees 8:4: to remember the unlawful destruction of innocent infants and the blasphemies committed against His name, and to show His hatred of wickedness.
units.2 Maccabees 8:5: Once Maccabeus had formed his company, he became irresistible to the nations, the Lord’s anger having turned to mercy.
